claims.statement: A finite set $\mathcal H\subset\mathbb N$ is \emph{admissible} if for every prime $q$ there is a residue class modulo $q$ containing no element of $\mathcal H$.

For a predicate $P$ on $\mathbb N$ and $k\ge j\ge1$, let $\DHL_P[k,j]$ be the statement: for every admissible $\mathcal H$ with $|\mathcal H|=k$ there are infinitely many $n$ such that $\#\{h\in\mathcal H: P(n+h)\}\ge j$. Write $\DHL[k,j]$ for $\DHL_P[k,j]$ with $P$ = primality.
For $c\in\mathbb N$ write $H_1\le c$ for the statement that $p_{n+1}-p_n\le c$ for infinitely many $n$. For an integer-valued sequence this is equivalent to $\liminf_{n}(p_{n+1}-p_n)\le c$.
For all $n\ge2$, $p_{n+1}-p_n\ge2$ and $p_{n+1}-p_n$ is even. Consequently $H_1\ge2$, and $H_1\le3$ if and only if $p_{n+1}-p_n=2$ for infinitely many $n$.
Let $P(n)$ hold if and only if $n\bmod4\in\{0,1\}$. Then $\DHL_P[3,2]$ holds (indeed for every $3$-element set), but $P(n)\wedge P(n+2)$ holds for no $n$; in particular $\DHL_P[2,2]$ fails.
A given sieve method establishes $\DHL[k,j]$ only if $j\le\lceil k/2\rceil$.
claims.title: Parity barrier

claims.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item Under \cref{hyp:parity}, a sieve method establishing $\DHL[k,2]$ has $k\ge3$. \item (Unconditional.) No admissible $3$-element set is contained in an interval $[a,a+5]$. Together with \cref{lem:adm}, the minimal diameter of an admissible $3$-set is exactly $6$. \end{enumerate}

56d42291f91e.question: Paper claim Theorem 3.1 (thm:gaps) states: “For all $n\ge2$, $p_{n+1}-p_n\ge2$ and $p_{n+1}-p_n$ is even. Consequently $H_1\ge2$, and $H_1\le3$ if and only if $p_{n+1}-p_n=2$ for infinitely many $n$.”. Lean theorem `two_le_gap` assumes `1 ≤ n` (n ≥ 1), but the claim says n ≥ 2. Is this an intentional indexing convention or a genuine change of domain?
56d42291f91e.answer: equivalent, intentional: index shift only. Lean `p` is 0-indexed (DHL32/Basic.lean:9, p 0 = 2) while the paper is 1-indexed (DHL32_note.tex:48, p_1 = 2), so Lean n >= 1 is exactly paper n >= 2. (two_le_gap)

Consequently $H_1\ge2$, and $H_1\le3$ if and only if $p_{n+1}-p_n=2$ for infinitely many $n$.”. Lean lemma `gap_even` assumes `1 ≤ n` (n ≥ 1), but the claim says n ≥ 2. cc5e051f3e37.answer: equivalent, intentional: index shift only. Lean `p` is 0-indexed (DHL32/Basic.lean:9, p 0 = 2) while the paper is 1-indexed (DHL32_note.tex:48, p_1 = 2), so Lean n >= 1 is exactly paper n >= 2. (gap_even)

382682972d36.question: Paper claim Theorem 3.3 (thm:model) states: “Let $P(n)$ hold if and only if $n\bmod4\in\{0,1\}$. Then $\DHL_P[3,2]$ holds (indeed for every $3$-element set), but $P(n)\wedge P(n+2)$ holds for no $n$; in particular $\DHL_P[2,2]$ fails.”. The matched Lean statement(s) `Ptoy_DHL32`, `Ptoy_no_twin`, `dhl32_not_implies_dhl22_combinatorially` do not mention the set {0,1}. Is the omission intentional, or is it covered by a declaration the matcher missed?
382682972d36.answer: equivalent, intentional: for n : ℕ, n % 4 ∈ {0,1,2,3}, so n % 4 < 2 ↔ n % 4 ∈ {0,1}; the paper's P(n) :⇔ n mod 4 ∈ {0,1} (DHL32_note.tex:94) is Lean's Ptoy (Theorems34.lean:25). Local branch pipelinehalt/align-wording adds Ptoy_iff_mod_four_mem stating this equivalence.

title: Resolving a category error: DHL[3,2] yields H1 <= 6, not H1 = 2 (B. S. Frohman, 2026)
